item.title: MLBB redeem codes: where to enter them and why a code fails
item.description: Step-by-step redemption on the official MOONTON page, where to find your Game ID and Zone ID, why a code fails and how to spot a scam site.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
MLBB redeem codes are entered on the official page mobilelegends.com/redeem, not inside the game.
You need four fields: the code, your Game ID, Zone ID and a verification code sent to your in-game mail.
The verification code is valid for 30 minutes. The reward arrives in your in-game mail.
You never need your account password to redeem a code. A site that asks for it is a scam.
Mobile Legends has no redeem field inside the game, so many players look for it in the settings and never find it. Codes are entered on the MOONTON website in the Redeem game rewards section. Below is a step-by-step guide to the official form and why a code may fail. There is no list of “working codes” here: they cannot be checked in advance, and codes from unofficial lists have usually expired.
Where to enter a redeem code
Fields of the official form at mobilelegends.com/redeem
Field
What to enter
Where to find it
Redemption code
The code itself
From the official source that gave it out
Game ID
Your account number
In-game profile: the ID line next to your name
Zone ID
Your server number
Same place, the number in brackets after the Game ID
Verification Code
A confirmation code
Sent to your in-game mail after you press Send
How to redeem a code, step by step
Open your in-game profile and note two numbers: the Game ID and the Zone ID in brackets, for example 123456789 (1234).
Go to mobilelegends.com/redeem and pick the site language if needed.
Paste the code into Redemption code, then enter your Game ID and Zone ID.
Press Send. Open your in-game mail: the verification code arrives there and is valid for 30 minutes.
Enter the verification code on the site and press Redeem. The reward arrives in your in-game mail.
The official form never asks for your password, email or Moonton ID details. If a “free diamonds” site asks you to log in, close it: that is how accounts get stolen.
Safety
Why a redeem code does not work
The code has expired. Every code has its own deadline, after which it is no longer accepted.
The code has run out. Many codes have a limited number of activations.
The code was already used on this account. The same code will not work twice.
The code is for another region or event. Some codes may work only on certain servers.
A typo in the Game ID or Zone ID. Check both numbers in your profile, especially the server number in brackets.
The verification code is stale. If more than 30 minutes have passed, press Send again.
Where to find real redeem codes
MOONTON hands out real codes itself: in the game’s official communities, during major tournaments and at special events. If a code appears on a list site without a link to its source, check the date and never enter it anywhere except mobilelegends.com/redeem. Services that “generate” codes or diamonds do not exist.
We do not publish code lists: a code cannot be checked without redeeming it on your own account, and outdated lists only waste time. If MOONTON releases a code for all players, we will cover it in the news with a link to the source.

item.title: Current MLBB patch: update 2.2.16 and what it changed
item.description: The key points of patch 2.2.16: the new Masha and Bruno, buffs and nerfs, match economy, the 2026 map and what happened to heroes two months later.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
The current MLBB patch is 2.2.16. It came out on 16 September 2026 together with the start of Season 42.
For the game’s 10th anniversary Masha and Bruno were reworked, and six more heroes got new models: Paquito, Kadita, Clint, Luo Yi, Brody and Badang.
Aulus, Argus, Aldous and Lukas were buffed; Miya, Hanabi, Melissa, Yi Sun-shin and Paquito were nerfed.
The next major patch is expected with Season 43: the last two arrived on the first day of a season, 17 June and 16 September.
Update 2.2.16 is the latest major Mobile Legends patch as of 22 November 2026. The developers lifted weak junglers and EXP lane heroes, fully reworked Masha and Bruno and slowed the match economy so a team that falls behind can come back more easily. Below are the key points from the official patch notes and how those changes look in the statistics two months later.

The rework landed harder than expected: Masha now has the highest win rate in the game at 60.47%. Argus climbed to 56.76% after his buff. Hanabi was nerfed but is still the most picked hero and wins 52.64%. Tigreal got a shorter cooldown on his second skill, yet his win rate remains one of the lowest at 45.20%.
The new Masha and the new Bruno
Masha is now a berserker fighter built for long fights rather than an assassin for split-pushing. She still has three HP bars, and attacking from the side of the wound she left triggers Feral: three wide claw strikes plus Resilience, Attack Speed and Movement Speed.
Masha’s second skill resets its cooldown each time she loses one of her lives.
Bruno keeps his ball-kicking marksman style, but the ball is easier to control: its distance scales with Movement Speed, it stays on the ground for 3 seconds instead of 2 and no longer crosses walls.
Bruno’s ultimate now briefly stuns the first target, slows it heavily and knocks it back to his attack range.
Match economy and the 2026 map
Gold from the Horned Lizard, Fire Beetle and Lava Golem is down 13%.
The comeback kill bounty now triggers at a 1500 gold deficit instead of 2000.
Minion gold grows a little more slowly over time.
Since 28 September the annual map update is live: vision wisps reveal hidden enemies, the Turtle spawns an allied turtle on a lane instead of a shield, and destroying turrets gives the whole team much more gold.
MOONTON says matches were too fast and teams that fell behind struggled to come back. In ranked this means a gold lead is less safe: games more often go the distance, and late-game mistakes cost more.
What it means in ranked
Modes, season and other changes
VS A.I. and Custom matches unlock at Elite rank, Magic Chess at level 12 and 1 VS 1 at level 25.
A Multiplayer Training Camp was added: Mode — VS A.I. & Custom — Multiplayer Training Camp.
The player Namecard was reworked: you can show a 3D hero model and arrange cards with your Mythic medal, collection and achievements.
The Season 42 skin is Flamehide Thane for Popol and Kupa, and the avatar border is Starward Decade.
When the next patch comes out
The last two major updates, 2.1.88 (17 June) and 2.2.16 (16 September), arrived on the day a new season started. Season 42 is expected to end on 16 December, so the next big patch will most likely come then. There is no official date yet. Once it is out, we will update this guide and the hero tier list.

item.title: Mobile Legends ranks in order: all tiers, stars and Mythic
item.description: A table of every MLBB rank in order, how many stars it takes to reach Mythic, how Mythic ranks work, placement and star protection.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
Mobile Legends has 10 ranks: Warrior, Elite, Master, Grandmaster, Epic, Legend, Mythic, Mythical Honor, Mythical Glory and Mythical Immortal.
You need 112 stars to reach Mythic, most of them in Grandmaster, Epic and Legend — 25 each.
Mythic has no divisions: Honor starts at 25 stars, Glory at 50 and Immortal at 100.
The first 10 Mythic matches are placement: a win gives two stars and a loss removes none.
The MLBB ranked ladder has two parts. The first six ranks are split into divisions, from III or V down to I, with 3–5 stars each. A win adds a star, a loss removes one, and when a division is full the next win moves you up. Mythic starts the second part: stars simply add up, and the rank name changes at 25, 50 and 100 stars.

Mobile Legends ranks from lowest to highest

The first ranks are the shortest: Warrior takes 9 stars and Elite 12. The real work starts in Grandmaster: three ranks in a row with 25 stars each, and that is where new players most often get stuck.
Mythic ranks and placement
After Legend I the next win takes you to Mythic. Placement starts here: 10 matches where every win gives two stars and a loss takes none. Placement can add up to 10 stars. After that stars again change by one per win or loss.

Stars add up with no cap
Out of 2,289 orders BOOST MLBB has completed since November 2025, 569 were stars inside Mythical Immortal and 343 inside Mythical Glory. The most common route between ranks is Glory to Immortal: 179 orders.
Where our customers play
How stars are gained and lost
A ranked win adds one star and a loss removes one.
The star protection bar fills up when you play well. When it is full, your next loss does not cost a star.
In Epic and Legend good matches also build star raising points: when the bar fills, you get an extra star.
In Mythic placement a win gives two stars, and a loss uses a match but removes no stars.
How many matches it takes to reach Mythic
Win rate decides everything. At 50% wins your stars barely move: losses cancel the wins, and only star protection pushes you forward. Every extra five percent of wins cuts the road several times. We estimated the number of matches including star protection and placement.
Approximate matches at different win rates
Assumptions: star protection triggers about once in six losses, and star raising points give a star every 35–50 matches. This is an estimate, not a game rule.

What happens to your rank at season end
A season lasts about three months. At the end your rank drops: Mythical Immortal and Mythical Glory start the new season in Legend V, Mythical Honor in Epic I and Mythic in Epic II. Rewards follow the highest rank you reached that season. We covered the expected end of Season 42 and the full reset chart in a separate guide.

item.title: When MLBB Season 42 ends and where your rank drops after the reset
item.description: The expected end of Season 42, the rank reset chart, season rewards and what happens to orders in the first days of a new season.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
Season 42 is expected to end on 16 December 2026. Moonton has not announced the date in advance; it is estimated from past season lengths.
At the reset Mythical Immortal and Mythical Glory drop to Legend V, Mythical Honor to Epic I and Mythic to Epic II.
Season rewards follow the highest rank you reached during the season, not your rank on the last day.
To get the season skin you need to play 20 ranked matches.
Season 42 started on 16 September 2026, the day update 2.2.16 came out. Recent seasons lasted about 91 days, so the end is expected on 16 December, with Season 43 opening the same day. This is an estimate from past seasons: there is no official date yet. The game itself is the most accurate source — ranked mode shows a timer with the days left in the season.
When Season 42 ends
What is known about Season 42 and 43 timing as of 22 November 2026
Season 41 lasted 91 days. If Moonton announces a different time, we will update the table.

Same estimate: a new season opens right after the old one
Usual season length
about 91 days
Average length of recent seasons
Season length varies: Season 40 ran for 98 days and Season 39 for 84 days. MOONTON ran the last changeover like this: Season 41 closed on 15 September at 21:59:59 server time, and Season 42 opened on 16 September at 00:00:00. So do not leave your last stars for 15 December. If the in-game timer shows a different date, trust the timer.
Where your rank drops after the reset
Rank reset at the start of a new season
MLBB Hub chart, checked at the reset between Seasons 40 and 41. Some players report different results, so check the in-game notice at the start of the season for your exact position.

Immortal and Glory players lose the most: hundreds of stars turn into Legend V. The way back is shorter than it looks: 25 Legend stars and Mythic placement, where a win in the first 10 matches gives two stars. Below Legend the reset is softer — Epic drops one or two divisions, and Warrior and Elite do not drop.
Which rewards a season gives
The reward follows the highest rank you reached during the season. If you were Mythic and fell back to Legend, you still get the Mythic reward.
The Season 42 skin is Flamehide Thane for Popol and Kupa. It requires 20 ranked matches.
Battle Points and tickets are given at every rank, and the amount grows with the rank.
The first week of a new season is the busiest. In the week Season 42 started, BOOST MLBB customers placed 102 orders against 30–40 in a normal summer week. Season 41 looked the same: 67 orders in its first week. Players want their rank back fast, and fewer boosters are free on those days.
What we see after every reset
What to do before the season ends
Open ranked mode and check the timer: the in-game date beats any forecast.
If you are a few stars short of the next rank, get them before 15 December — the reward follows your highest rank.
Finish 20 ranked matches if you have not yet and want the season skin.
If you plan a boost after the reset, order on the first day: the queue grows after that.
How stars, divisions and Mythic thresholds work is covered in our separate guide to Mobile Legends ranks in order. It also shows how many matches the road to Mythic usually takes at different win rates.
